summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR853 million from INR1,024 million, with EBITDA at negative INR149 million and a net loss of INR176 million.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations declined YoY as Middle East conflict supply-chain disruptions hit S&P and trading execution for most of the quarter. Management attributed roughly INR50-55 crore of revenue impact to the quarter and expects execution to normalise by end-Q2 FY27. Order book rose to INR699 crore, mainly on S&P orders, and management guides to an order intake of about INR1,000 crore for FY27. Strategic moves included a small stake in WaHa with India and UAE rights, a first European ZLD order, and continued traction for the H-Xtreme heat exchanger.

segments.name: S&P (services and products)
segments.commentary: Most affected by supply-chain disruption in Q1; the order book increase was primarily driven by S&P orders. Management did not give a segment revenue figure.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Revenue lost of about INR15 crore in the quarter due to the disruption.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: About INR42-43 crore of orders were delayed or down in the quarter.

segments.name: Roserve (Water as a Service)
segments.commentary: Management said it is performing well with marquee projects in execution and aims to build recurring, annuity-style revenue; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Execution expected to normalise by end-Q2 FY27; management said Q2 should show growth but remains subject to developments over the next six weeks.
Order book of INR699 crore; management said 80-85% conversion in FY27 would yield growth for the year.
FY27 order intake target of about INR1,000 crore, with large domestic and international orders expected to convert over the next three to four months.
EBITDA margin historically 14-16%; temporary margin pressure from talent and execution investment, expected to stabilise once growth crosses about INR850 crore.
Medium-term guidance of 20-25% growth with EBITDA margin of 12-16% over the next two to three years (management's stated range).
capex_capacity: First project delivered with new REM membranes in partnership with NALA Membranes, targeting textile and paper effluent.
Steel ZLD orders worth INR1,430 million signed, including INR1,260 million from a large Indian steel manufacturer; management described it as one of the largest ZLD orders in India.
Waste pickle liquor treatment solution demonstrated at a large steel manufacturer; management expects conversion to an order within two months.
Semiconductor entry via a US partner with a Micron collaboration; initial focus on membrane replacement, then project segment.
No capex amounts or capacity figures disclosed.
risks_watch: Execution recovery depends on supply-chain stability through the next six weeks and into H2; management flagged ongoing industry-wide execution challenges.
EBITDA was negative INR149 million, and management expects margin pressure from investments in talent and large projects.
Revenue for Q1 fell YoY and the company posted a net loss versus a profit a year earlier.
WaHa opportunity has no revenue or size disclosed yet; stake is under 2%.
Order intake target of about INR1,000 crore requires converting large domestic and international pipeline in the next three to four months.
Management said margin and growth guidance will depend on the outcome of large-project execution and market developments.
key_quotes: Our revenue performance during the quarter was impacted by supply chain disruptions due to the conflict in the Middle East for the better part of the quarter.
Our order book has increased to INR699 crores primarily on the back of S &P order book, providing strong revenue visibility for the quarters to come.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost in Q1 due to the disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading lost about INR15 crore of revenue and manufacturing had about INR42-43 crore of orders totally down; overall impact about INR50-55 crore for the quarter, with S&P the segment mainly impacted.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 be degrowth or flat, and how should H2 and full-year growth look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply chains are getting back to normal with freight and spare part costs easing since July, and Q2 should end up in a growth phase, subject to the next six weeks. With 80-85% conversion of the INR699 crore order book, management said the company has the ability to exceed and deliver growth this year, with H2 dependent on execution stability.

qa_highlights.question: Size, margins and revenue timing of the European ZLD order?
qa_highlights.answer: Order is roughly EUR600,000 for a metal slag value-recovery project, with delivery expected in Q3 FY27; margins expected to be good as export margins exceed local ones, but exact numbers too early to give.

qa_highlights.question: Margin and growth outlook for next years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 14-16% EBITDA margin historically; temporary pressure from talent and large-project execution investment, expected to stabilise after growth crosses about INR850 crore. Guided 20-25% growth with 12-16% EBITDA margin over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity size and revenue expectations from the WaHa partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: No numbers yet; applications cited include data-centre dehumidification and battery manufacturing, and management hopes to share more details by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Stake size and capital invested in WaHa?
qa_highlights.answer: Stake is less than 2%, for about USD575,000, and is largely a licensing arrangement with exclusivity for India and UAE.

demand_pricing: Order book at INR699 crore, increase driven mainly by S&P order book; management said a significant portion is deliverable in FY27 and 80-85% conversion would yield growth for the year.
Revenue impact from Middle East supply-chain disruption about INR50-55 crore for the quarter: trading about INR15 crore lost, manufacturing about INR42-43 crore of orders totally down.

Steel ZLD orders of INR1,430 million signed, including INR1,260 million from a large Indian steel manufacturer; waste pickle liquor solution demonstrated at a large steel maker with conversion to order expected within two months.
First European ZLD order, about EUR600,000, metal slag value-recovery project; delivery expected in Q3 FY27; management said export margins are better than domestic but too early to quantify.

FY27 order intake target about INR1,000 crore, about INR200 crore already secured; large domestic and international orders expected to convert over next three to four months. Management cited a pipeline of about INR3,200 crore.
Management named alcohol beverage and steel as largest order book sectors, followed by pharmaceuticals and chemicals; first solar orders under execution. Industry-wise breakup to be sent offline.
Competition in ZLD named as Ion Exchange, Thermax, Arvind Envisol, Praj Engineering, Permionics and Hyper Filtration; management said an industry survey placed it just below Ion Exchange in ZLD.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book conversion and recovery to growth, but explicitly cautious that Q2 and H2 execution depend on supply-chain stability over the next six weeks. Evasive or deferred on quantification: no segment revenue, WaHa size, European order margins, or industry-wise order breakup (offered offline).

growth.why: Management guides 20-25% medium-term growth and FY27 order intake of about INR1,000 crore (about INR200 crore secured, INR699 crore order book, INR3,200 crore pipeline), but Q1 revenue fell about 17% YoY on a INR50-55 crore Middle East disruption and no capacity additions or capex were disclosed.
